problem: Sales were weak at the launch price of $699.
title: Juicero sells a $399 connected juicer and shuts down after 16 months
context: Juicero raised about $120 million from investors and sold a Wi-Fi juice press that used proprietary produce packs.
decision_made: Cut the price to $399 in January 2017, then suspend sales and close the company on 1 September 2017.
action_taken: Offered refunds with requests due by 1 December 2017; Bloomberg's April 2017 report showed packs could be squeezed by hand nearly as effectively.
observed_outcome: The company stopped operating after about 16 months on sale. Bloomberg attributed the collapse to unsustainable costs, unflattering headlines and a bungled launch.
lessons: A complex, costly product can fail when a simple alternative does nearly the same job.
limitations: The video detail in some accounts was not confirmed. The company's stated reasons were about distribution infrastructure and may be only part of the cause.

claims.claim_text: Juicero announced on 1 September 2017 that it was shutting down and suspending sales of its press.
Bloomberg's postmortem attributed the collapse to unsustainable costs, unflattering headlines and a bungled launch.
